_note:
Labelled set for scripts/eval-matcher.js and scripts/tune-flag-thresholds.js. One profile, thirty postings. `recorded` is a DeepSeek answer captured once and committed, so the offline run is deterministic and measures THIS repository's flag handling, span finding and ranking rather than today's weather at DeepSeek. Re-record with scripts/record-eval.ts --deepseek when the prompt changes.

TWO LABEL FIELDS, AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.

`expect.flags` is what a correct matcher should RAISE, and it is DeepSeek's contract: the scoring prompt tells it to raise a code only when it can point at something in the posting, so a code that is true but unquotable does not belong here. eval-matcher.js scores precision and recall against this field and treats anything outside it as a false positive.

`expect.codes` is what is TRUE of the posting, one entry per flag code, labelled against the exact question wording in supabase/functions/_shared/judge.ts. It exists because Jev is asked all ten questions on every posting and must answer each one, while `expect.flags` only ever listed the one or two codes a case was built to exercise. Reading an absent code as false is what made a flag-threshold sweep meaningless: `open` scored 0.17 precision against flags on 2026-09-28 almost entirely because nine cases that never mentioned openness were counted as negatives.

So a code is present here only when the posting DETERMINES it. A code the posting leaves genuinely open is OMITTED, and the sweep skips it rather than counting it either way. The labelling rules, which are what make an omission auditable:
  comp  true on a signal of unusual applicant volume, a mass-market employer, or explicit selectivity language (a firm that says it recruits only from a narrow set of institutions is describing a competitive process, not a quiet one). An obscure employer with no such language is a FALSE rather than an omission: obscurity is evidence against unusual competition, not an absence of evidence. Omitted only where the posting does not identify the employer at all.
  open  true only on explicit text welcoming non-traditional backgrounds (no degree needed, self-taught, blind process); false where the posting demands conventional pedigree or a degree; omitted on silence.
  rare  true only where the posting asks for BOTH payments/fintech domain depth AND hands-on platform or infrastructure ownership, since that pair is the profile's unusual_combination; false otherwise.
  fit   judged on the work alone, can-do and targeting, independent of whether the candidate is eligible. A role ruled out by location can still be a true `fit` here; it is `loc` that carries the disqualification.
  loc   carries geographic ineligibility, including work-authorisation gates. `cred` is for credentials, not geography.
  cred  a formal credential the candidate lacks (a degree, a certification, a clearance). An experience or skill bar is NOT a credential, however hard it is to clear.
  thin  true when the decisive facts are absent, regardless of length: thin-culture-copy is four sentences and true, thin-one-line-stack is one sentence and false.

Where the two fields disagree on purpose, the case carries `expect.codes_note` saying why.

Every case carries `set`. The holdout is never tuned on and is the only honest input to a final comparison; the tune set is where work happens. Holdout membership is checked by tune-flag-thresholds.js, which refuses to report a threshold for a code whose tune set does not hold both labels.

expect.band_note: This band contradicts sen-lo-junior's [40,100] and the contradiction is deliberate rather than overlooked. The two postings are materially the same -- a remote-India graduate role stating that no prior experience is required -- and DeepSeek scored reachability 5 here against 70 there. Both cannot be right. Low is the defensible answer, since an over-levelled applicant is screened out rather than hired, which makes sen-lo-junior's band the one to revisit. It is left alone here because relabelling a committed case to match a later opinion is how a baseline stops meaning anything.
